findings.title: Plan-verification recommendation lacks structured provenance for its claims
findings.what: The recommendation claims a precise flagged/total percentage, threshold crossings, absence of Verification/Test sections, and that these plans are “most likely to ship under-specified,” but `evidence` contains only up to five names and the result has no `provenance`. Consumers therefore cannot reproduce the quantitative claim from cited artifact fields, and the comparative risk assertion has no supporting observation or qualified inference.
findings.fix: Add structured provenance observations citing each relevant plan artifact and the `fileRefs`, `words`, and `hasVerification` fields, plus aggregate flagged/total values. Remove the “most likely” assertion or explicitly qualify it as an inference supported by recorded evidence.
findings.acceptance: A detector test validates recommendation provenance and asserts that the emitted observations identify the source plan(s), threshold-driving fields and values, and flagged/total calculation; no unsupported comparative-risk wording remains.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read src/lib/detectors/workflow/plan-missing-verification.ts:34-59 and confirmed the returned object has names-only evidence and no provenance. The directly related PlanSignature baseline type exposes only name/id, sections, fileRefs, words, and hasVerification, so it supplies no independent evidence for the “most likely” claim.
